status: subvariant concept proposals, awaiting visual feedback; not production sprites
scope: Two new proposals for each selected family A/C/F; original selected concepts retained as A1/C1/F1.
commonPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE new concept sprite variation of a modular isometric wall for a mobile dark fantasy dungeon.
Input1 is the SELECTED FAMILY CONCEPT: preserve its slate blue hand-painted art direction, soft chunky bevels, proportions and family character. Input2 is the CURRENT PRODUCTION WALL: preserve its camera orientation and approximately its overall volume/end connection profiles.
View: strict 2:1 dimetric isometric, long wall slopes down-right, upper surfaces and small right end visible. Exactly TWO masonry courses; the visible top plane belongs to the upper course, not an extra row. Keep wall height, thickness and overall length consistent. No pillar, footings, floor or extra cap.
Mobile readability: calm broad painted planes, restrained contrast, meaningful large silhouette/joint variation at 114 pixels wide, no microtexture or grain. Match selected concept lighting from upper-left. Actual transparent background and transparent padding on every side. No external shadow, backdrop, glow cloud, labels, text or frame.
This is a newly drawn variation within an approved concept family, not a mirror, rotation or recolour of the reference. These are concept proposals; precise wireframe end matching will follow separately.

jobs.label: A2 · Pierre longue en haut
jobs.detail: Maçonnerie décalée family. Make the UPPER course two large unequal stones: a long stone taking about 62% of the run on the left and a shorter right stone. The LOWER course has four unequal stones, roughly 18%, 29%, 21%, 32%, so its three joints never align with the upper joint. All stones flush to the wall, clean and softly bevelled. Different from reference's four upper and three lower blocks. No relief boss, damage, carving, roots or crystals.

jobs.label: C2 · Deux reliefs décalés
jobs.detail: Blocs en relief family. Replace the reference's single large centered upper boss with TWO modest raised chamfered stones of different widths, diagonally separated: an upper stone around the left third and a lower stone around the right two-thirds. Each is an actual masonry block projecting slightly toward viewer, with broad bevels and a quiet flat center, not a pasted plaque. Remaining blocks stay flush; terminal blocks stay simple to allow later joins. Exactly two courses throughout. No carved diamond, symbol, purple, roots or extra column.

jobs.label: C3 · Relief large en bas
jobs.detail: Blocs en relief family. Exactly two main masonry courses. Keep upper course plain and flush with three unequal stones. LOWER course has ONE wide, low stone slightly off-center toward the left, projecting toward viewer with a broad pillow-like chamfer and softly octagonal face, integrated as the stone itself. Lower side stones remain flush. This has a different low horizontal silhouette and relief location from reference's top central rectangular boss. Keep the bottom baseline straight and terminal profiles simple. No pedestal, third course, insignia, carving, roots or crystal.

jobs.label: F2 · Racines étalées
jobs.detail: Pierre corrompue family. Redesign corruption as a LOW, ASYMMETRIC HORIZONTAL ROOT spreading along the middle joint from left-of-center toward the right, with one curling branch around the lower middle stone and two short offshoots. ONE small violet crystal is nestled in a lower joint toward the right, and most stone remains bare. Root topology must differ from reference's tall central vertical branching cluster: no central Y shape. Crystal and roots have dark purple volumes and localized violet edges, no broad glow. Root ends taper naturally within the segment rather than crossing terminals; keep same two-course wall. Optional surface ornament visually integrates into mortar without destroying the bare structural wall. No new hole, niche or broken wall.

jobs.label: F3 · Cristaux et racines courtes
jobs.detail: Pierre corrompue family. Redesign corruption as a COMPACT ASYMMETRIC CLUSTER of three small differently sized violet crystal shards at the upper-right internal joint, safely inside the end stone boundary, surrounded by a few SHORT CURVED DARK ROOTS hugging adjacent joints. One fine branch trails down toward the middle; the left half stays bare. Clear compact crystal grouping, not reference's single center crystal/large branching root and not a long horizontal root. Keep any projection below the top surface, maintain straight overall top/bottom, two masonry courses. Muted amethyst accent with restrained localized light, no neon fissure, Y mark, particles or glow cloud. Roots/crystals are optional surface ornaments, not a structural hole.
